edits.old: Pointcloud's 61,952-pixel focal-plane array (FPA, §C10.4) could fill its field only with a mode-equivalent collecting diameter of ≈0.8 mm. At an assumed nominal footprint fraction of ≈2%, the identity allows ≈6 mm. [E: the bound is the identity Eq. (140), derived in item 4, with $f_{\rm fp}\le1$ and a cell solid angle $\theta_{\rm cell}^2=\Omega_{\rm FOV}/N_{\rm cell}$, where $N_{\rm cell}=61{,}952$ is the number of pixels and $\Omega_{\rm FOV}$ the 23° × 14° field: $A_{\rm mode}\lesssim\tfrac{t^2}{2}N_{\rm cell}\lambda^2/\Omega_{\rm FOV}=0.42\times61{,}952\times(1.31\ \mu{\rm m})^2/[(23^\circ\times14^\circ)(\pi/180)^2]=0.42\times61{,}952\times1.72\times10^{-12}/0.098=0.45$ mm². That is an equivalent diameter $2\sqrt{A_{\rm mode}/\pi}=0.76$ mm; at $f_{\rm fp}=0.02$ it becomes $0.45/0.02=23$ mm², or 5.4 mm. Using the 0.061° address pitch $\theta_{\rm cell}$ instead of the quoted field, $\tfrac{t^2}{2}(\lambda/\theta_{\rm cell})^2=0.64$ mm², gives 0.9 mm and 6.4 mm.]
edits.new: Pointcloud's 61,952-pixel focal-plane array (FPA, §C10.4) could fill its field only with a mode-equivalent collecting diameter of ≈0.9 mm behind its 50 mm lens. The one beam its authors measured, behind a 25 mm test lens focused at 11.1 m [P, Settembrini et al. 2026, Methods and Extended Data Fig. 2c], has a nominal 1/e² footprint fraction of ≈1% at that focus and ≈2% at 22 m on that lens's 0.12° address grid, and hence a mode-equivalent collecting diameter of ≈5 mm and ≈3.5 mm. [E: the full-coverage bound is the identity Eq. (140), derived in item 4, with $f_{\rm fp}\le1$. For the 0.061° address pitch of the 50 mm lens, $\theta_{\rm cell}=53\ \mu{\rm m}/50\ {\rm mm}=1.06\times10^{-3}$ rad, it gives $A_{\rm mode}\lesssim\tfrac{t^2}{2}(\lambda/\theta_{\rm cell})^2=0.42\times(1.31\ \mu{\rm m}/1.06\times10^{-3})^2=0.64$ mm², an equivalent diameter $2\sqrt{A_{\rm mode}/\pi}=0.9$ mm. Spreading the $N_{\rm cell}=61{,}952$ cells over the measured 23.1° × 13.6° field instead, $\theta_{\rm cell}^2=\Omega_{\rm FOV}/N_{\rm cell}$, gives 0.47 mm² (0.77 mm), because that field includes the routing gaps between pixel blocks: 352 × 176 pixels at 0.061° span only 21.4° × 10.7°. The measured beam has $w(R)=w_0\sqrt{1+[(R-11.1\ {\rm m})/z_R]^2}$ with $w_0=1.31$ mm and $z_R=4.1$ m. On the 25 mm lens's pitch, $\theta_{\rm cell}=53\ \mu{\rm m}/25\ {\rm mm}=2.12\times10^{-3}$ rad, its footprint fraction $f_{\rm fp}=\pi w^2/(R\theta_{\rm cell})^2$ is $5.39\ {\rm mm^2}/(23.5\ {\rm mm})^2=1.0\%$ at 11.1 m and, with $w=3.72$ mm, $43.5\ {\rm mm^2}/(46.6\ {\rm mm})^2=2.0\%$ at 22 m. Eq. (33) of §C0 with $t=1$, as in §C0 subsection 10.8, gives $A_{\rm mode}=\lambda^2R^2/(2\pi w^2)=19.6$ mm² (5.0 mm) at 11.1 m and 9.6 mm² (3.5 mm) at 22 m; each times its $f_{\rm fp}$ is $\tfrac12(\lambda/\theta_{\rm cell})^2=0.19$ mm², as Eq. (140) requires.]

edits.new: On Argoverse 2 the vehicle AP of FSD (a fully sparse 3D detector, unrelated to Tesla's FSD software), averaged over 0.5–4 m centre-distance match thresholds, falls from **89.0 to 61.7, 29.2, 13.9 and 3.6** across 0–50 / 50–100 / 100–150 / 150–200 / 200–250 m. edits.new: In nuScenes (32 beams), about **a third of the annotated objects at 50–80 m have zero lidar points**: 45,050 of 145,173 training boxes and 10,069 of 31,727 validation boxes (Gupta et al., Far3Det, WACV 2023, appendix Table 11). edits.old: Piggott et al. (Waymo) put coherent detection about 6 dB behind ToF at equal aperture, from polarization and mode weighting [P]; the far-field factor of item 2 in this model is 2.9×, or 4.7 dB.
edits.new: Piggott et al. (Waymo) put coherent detection about 6 dB behind ToF at long range: 3 dB for the single polarization and ≈3 dB because their 30 mm ToF lens, sized not to clip the coherent beam's Gaussian wings ($w_0=10$ mm), has $(15/10)^2=2.25$ times the coherent mode's far-field collecting area $\pi w_0^2$ before polarization [P, §2.5, Fig. 5(a)]. The far-field factor of item 2 in this model is 2.9×, or 4.7 dB, because its Gaussian fills the hard aperture more fully ($w_0=0.45D$, an aperture radius of $1.11w_0$ against $1.5w_0$) and pays 1.47× (1.7 dB) for mode shape and truncation instead of 2.25× (3.5 dB); the polarization factor is the same [E].
edits.why: Source found by the R6_C10_part2 research agent; see sources/R6_C10_part2_findings.md, R6_C10_part2-08.
